6.notes: Diagram description in the solution (single bar, hatched bottom section, plain middle section, dotted top section) matches the attached image exactly.

23.notes: Hints and solution are sound and match the diagram (X = MC, the AR=MR line at P, equilibrium at Q where rising MC cuts MR), but the subtopic placement is wrong for what the question actually tests. It is placed on 'costs.short-long-run (Theory of cost and revenue > Short-run and long-run costs): What the short run and long run are ... the shapes of short-run and long-run cost curves, and why the marginal cost curve above average variable cost is the firm's supply curve.' Nothing in that scope is about locating a profit-maximising equilibrium output by finding where MC=MR on a cost-and-revenue diagram; that is a market-equilibrium/profit topic, the same family as Q25's 'markets.profit-shutdown' (which explicitly covers 'reading the profit or loss area on a cost and revenue diagram'). The question is a firm-equilibrium question wearing a cost-curve-shape id.
23.fix: Reassign subtopic_id from costs.short-long-run to markets.profit-shutdown (or the taxonomy's nearest 'firm equilibrium / MC=MR' id), since the question tests locating profit-maximising equilibrium output on a cost-and-revenue diagram, not the shape of short-run/long-run cost curves or the MC-above-AVC supply curve result.

25.notes: The question stem as given is corrupted and a distractor is missing from 'Why not the others'. The options print as 'A. employ more labour / B. shut down completely. D. pay new allowances to its workers' with no 'C.' option at all, and B and D are run together on one line. The solution's 'Why not the others' section only has an 'A.' line and a 'D.' line (the D line is annotated '(printed inside option B in the source)'); there is no 'C.' line addressing the missing third distractor, so a distractor is left unaddressed, which fails check 4 regardless of whether the loss is upstream in the source scan. The shutdown-rule reasoning itself (AR below minimum AVC forces shutdown) is correct and not in question.
25.fix: Recover option C's text from the original WASSCE 2025 Economics paper and split the garbled line back into 'B. shut down completely' and 'D. pay new allowances to its workers' as separate options. Then add a corresponding line to Why not the others, e.g. 'C. <recovered option text>: <one clause saying why it fails>.' Do not invent option C's wording; pull it from the source paper.

37.notes: Hint 2 does the job of eliminating every distractor at once, so by the time the student reaches hint 3 the answer is already available by elimination, not by thinking. Exact text: "Borrowers repay loans with money that is worth less than when they borrowed it, so they tend to gain. Firms' money revenue and profits also tend to rise as prices rise." This confirms A (borrowers gain), C (dividends, via "profits also tend to rise") and D (sales revenue, via "firms' money revenue... rise") all in one line, leaving balance of payments as the only option not confirmed as a gainer. Hint 3 then adds nothing a student needs, since the choice was already made for them at hint 2.
37.fix: Borrowers repay loans with money that is worth less than when they borrowed it, so they are usually counted among the gainers from inflation. Now look at the other three: which one is not simply a sum of money that can go up when prices rise?

38.notes: Hint 2 eliminates all three distractors in one line, so hint 3 is answered before it is even read. Exact text: "A high rate of interest makes people want to put money where it earns interest, so they hold less idle cash. Payment arrangements and paydays mainly affect money held for everyday buying." This rules out A (interest rate) and, together, B and C (payment arrangements and paydays), leaving high degree of uncertainty as the only option standing. Hint 3 then only confirms what elimination already settled.
38.fix: A high rate of interest mainly affects the speculative motive: it makes people want to put idle cash where it earns interest. The precautionary motive is about something else entirely.

39.notes: Hint 2 eliminates all three distractors before hint 3 is reached. Exact text: "Notes and coins are legal tender. Money in a current account can be spent by cheque or transfer, so it counts as bank money." "Legal tender" clears both A (bank notes) and D (fiat coins), and the second sentence clears B (current account deposits), leaving promissory notes as the only option not confirmed as money. Hint 3 then has nothing left to narrow.
39.fix: Notes and coins are legal tender, so they are always accepted in payment. Think about how each of the other options gets its acceptance, if it has any at all.

40.notes: Hint 2 eliminates all three distractors in one line, leaving only the correct answer standing before hint 3 is read. Exact text: "Buildings, vehicles and equipment are things the bank owns, and loans are money customers owe the bank." This clears B (physical buildings and equipment), D (vehicle and office equipment) and C (loans granted to customers) together, leaving shareholders' funds as the only option not confirmed as an asset.
40.fix: Buildings and equipment are things the bank owns, so wherever they appear among the options they count as assets.

41.notes: Not a hint or solution defect, so it does not affect the verdict, but flagging for content ops: option B in the question text reads "Tover than proposed expenditure", which looks like a corrupted rendering of "Lower than proposed expenditure" (the solution itself correctly renders it as "Answer: B. lower than proposed expenditure"). Worth fixing at the source/import stage so the student does not see a nonsense word in the option list.
